title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook: Runbooks, Rotations, Game Days, Status Page & Comm Templates
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s standard incident process, runbook templates, postmortem expectations, on-call rotations, game-day guidance, status-page practices, and customer/internal communication templates. It is intended for engineers, on-call responders, SRE, and support teams.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-detect and time-to-recover for production incidents.
- Provide clear, repeatable runbooks for common failure modes.
- Standardize communications to customers and internal stakeholders.
- Maintain healthy on-call rotations and reduce burnout through tooling and clear handoffs.

1) Incident Severity Classification and Targets

Severity matrix (use the lowest severity that reflects customer impact):

| Severity | Short name | Definition | Initial page / Ping | Target Acknowledgement | Target Mitigation (Tactical) | Owner escalation |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Sev 1 | P0 | Production outage affecting large portion of customers or critical infrastructure (service down or > 50% error rate). | Pager duty immediate (primary on-call + #oncall-channel) | 5 minutes | Partial mitigation or rollback within 30–60 minutes | Eng SRE lead -> Engineering manager -> VP Eng |
| Sev 2 | P1 | Degraded performance or partial customer impact (e.g. elevated errors for subset of traffic). | Pager (on-call) + #oncall-channel | 15 minutes | Workaround within 2 hours | Secondary on-call -> Service owner -> EM |
| Sev 3 | P2 | Non-critical problems; single-customer issues; operational alerts requiring attention (no immediate customer impact). | Slack alert -> #oncall-channel | 2 hours | Fix in backlog sprint or hotfix 1–3 days | Service owner |
| Sev 4 | P3 | Informational or maintenance notices. | Ticket / email | N/A | Planned change | Service owner |

SLO/Alert thresholds (example):
- API success rate SLO: 99.95% monthly.
- Alert: 5xx rate > 0.5% for 5 continuous minutes -> Sev2.
- Alert: 5xx rate > 5% for 1 minute -> Sev1.
- P95 latency target breach for text generation (> 2x baseline) for 5 minutes -> Sev2.

2) Incident Process (High-level)

1. Detection & Triage
   - Alerts surface in PagerDuty and #oncall-channel. On-call engineer acknowledges within target acknowledgement window.
   - Triage: confirm scope (services, regions, customers), severity, initial mitigation steps.

2. Mobilize
   - If Sev1/Sev2: Create an incident in the incident tracker (Jira/Confluence incident page) with title: [SEV1] short-description — region/service.
   - Assign roles: Incident Lead, Scribe, Communications owner, Escalation owner.

3. Contain & Mitigate
   - Execute relevant runbooks (see section 3).
   - Apply short-term mitigations: scale up, circuit-break traffic, rollback model version, redirect traffic to fallback model/region.

4. Communicate
   - Use status page and customer templates for external comms (see section 7).
   - Post internal updates every 15–30 minutes for Sev1 until mitigated.

5. Resolve & Recover
   - Confirm recovery via metrics, logs, and synthetic tests.
   - Close incident when a stable state is reached and monitoring is green for the defined observation window (typically 60 minutes for Sev1).

6. Postmortem & Action Items
   - Owner creates postmortem within 72 hours (see section 5).
   - Track follow-up items with owners and due dates; prioritize remediation work in roadmap or reliability initiatives.

Roles & responsibilities
- Incident Lead: directs response, makes operational decisions.
- Scribe: documents timeline and actions in incident page.
- Communications owner: external/internal status updates.
- Secondary/Backup: technical support for escalations.
- Engineering Manager: approval for rollbacks or high-impact changes.

3) Runbook Template (single flat, copyable template)

Runbook: <short name>
- Service: <service-name>
- Impact: <symptoms / why it matters>
- Owner: <service owner / pager group>
- Pager: <pagerduty escalation policy>
- Preconditions: <required access, accounts, consoles, keys>
- Dashboard(s): <links to Grafana, Kibana, Datadog charts>
- Logs / Queries: <example log queries>
- Quick-check steps (ordered):
  1. Confirm alert and scope: run queries (example):
     - Datadog: avg(last_5m): sum:requests.errors{service:svc} / sum:requests.total{service:svc} > 0.05
     - Kibana query: service:svc AND response.status:500 AND @timestamp:[now-15m TO now]
  2. Check model-serving hosts for 10xx/timeout errors: ssh jump -> docker ps / systemctl status redwood-runtime
  3. Check GPU memory and KV cache pressure: nvidia-smi, monitoring charts.
  4. If recent deploy: check rollout status and revert to previous model/version if necessary.
  5. If API latency: increase replicas / scale up dedicated pool or route traffic to fallback model.
- Mitigation commands (examples):
  - kubectl get pods -n model-serving -l app=svc -o wide
  - kubectl rollout status deployment/svc --namespace=model-serving
  - kubectl scale deployment/svc --replicas=10 --namespace=model-serving
  - Deploy rollback: kubectl rollout undo deployment/svc --namespace=model-serving
- Temporary workarounds: circuit-break requests at ingress, enable degraded-mode config (feature toggle), reduce max tokens for requests to keep latency bounded.
- Recovery verification: synthetic requests to API, customer-sample requests, monitor error-rate and P95 for 30–60 minutes.
- Post-incident steps: open postmortem, attach timeline, note the runbook changes required, assign owners.

Example: Runbook for "Model service 5xx spike"
- Quick-check: confirm error spike, check recent model rollout, check GPU memory, check queue lengths.
- Common fixes: rollback model, scale replicas, clear inference queue, adjust batching and KV cache settings, apply rate-limits.

4) Escalation Matrix & Contacts
- Primary on-call: first responder (PagerDuty).
- Secondary: technical backup within 15 minutes if primary cannot mitigate.
- Eng SRE Lead: escalate if event impacts multiple services or > 30 minutes without mitigation.
- EM/Manager: decision on cross-team coordination, customer notifications, or postmortem reviewers.
- Exec on-call: optional for high-severity incidents requiring executive-level notifications.

Contact list (keep synced in team wiki):
- On-call schedule: link to roster (PagerDuty schedule).
- PagerDuty runbook link: https://pagerduty.example.com/teams/redwood-inference
- Slack channels: #oncall, #incidents, #prod-alerts

5) Postmortem Template & Expectations
- Create a postmortem page titled: Postmortem: [date] — [short-title] — [SEV].
- Required sections:
  - Summary: one-paragraph description of what happened and impact.
  - Timeline: minute-level timeline of detection, actions, mitigations, and recovery.
  - Root cause analysis: evidence-based RCA (avoid blame, focus on causal chain).
  - Contributing factors: telemetry gaps, configuration mistakes, process issues.
  - Remediation plan: specific action items, owners, and due dates.
  - Lessons learned: what we will do differently.
  - Severity and customer impact: number of customers affected, revenue risk, legal/regulatory risk.
- Postmortem cadence: must be created within 72 hours for Sev1/Sev2. A reviewer from Eng SRE and Product should sign off within 7 days.

6) On-call Rotations & Handoffs
- Rotation length: default 1-week rotations for primary on-call (Mon–Sun). Secondary coverage on weekdays 0800–2000 local office hours.
- Shift load: aim for no more than 1–2 high-sev incidents per rotation per engineer.
- Handoff checklist:
  - Confirm active incidents and outstanding action items.
  - Share recent alerts, ongoing mitigations, and paging noise patterns.
  - Update runbooks and dashboards used during rotation.
  - Confirm access keys and escalation contacts.
- Burnout controls: mandatory 2-week minimum between intensive rotations, optional rotation-swaps with manager approval, and rotational on-call compensation policy in People Ops.

7) Game Days & Exercises
- Purpose: validate runbooks, verify monitoring & alerting, practice communications and cross-team coordination.
- Frequency: quarterly for each major service (model-serving, API-gateway, routing/smart-router).
- Game day plan template:
  1. Objective & scope.
  2. Pre-game checklist: synthetic tests, baseline snapshots, participants and roles.
  3. Failure scenarios: (a) GPU farm OOM, (b) model rollout causing 5xx, (c) S3/feature store unavailability.
  4. Execution: inject failures or run tabletop exercise, observe detection and response.
  5. Debrief: document gaps, update runbooks, and assign follow-ups.
- Success metrics: mean time to detect (MTTD), mean time to recover (MTTR), completeness of runbook steps, communication cadence adherence.

8) Status Page & Communication Templates

Internal incident update cadence (Sev1): every 15 minutes until mitigated. Use the internal incident page to record updates.

External (Customer-facing) Status Page Template (short updates)
- Title: [Identified] — [Service] — Incident affecting [functionality]
- Summary: We are experiencing degraded [service] affecting [customers/regions]. Our engineers are investigating.
- Impact: What customers may see (errors, slow responses, degraded models).
- Mitigation: What we have done and immediate workaround (e.g., traffic routing, rollback).
- ETA / Next update: Provide an estimated time for next update.
- Link to status page: <link>

Customer email template (for major incidents)
Subject: [Redwood] Incident impacting [service] — [short summary]
Hi <Customer name>,
We detected an incident affecting [service] beginning at <time>. Impact: <brief impact summary>. Our engineering team is actively investigating and has applied immediate mitigations: <list>. We will provide updates every <interval> and notify you when service is fully restored. If you have dedicated support, your account team will follow up directly.
Regards,
Redwood Operations

Post-incident customer communication (example)
Subject: [Resolved] Incident affecting [service] on <date>
Hi <Customer name>,
The incident impacting [service] has been resolved as of <time>. Root cause: <short RCA>. Impact: <customers affected>. Actions taken: <rollback, fixes, config changes>. Follow-up: <planned remediation and timeline>. We apologize for the disruption and are taking steps to reduce recurrence.
Best,
Redwood Reliability Team

9) Runbook & Playbook Maintenance
- Ownership: each runbook must list an owner and quarterly review date.
- After-action updates: following any incident or game day, update runbooks within 7 days or mark them as needing a revision with an owner and due date.
- Audit: Eng SRE runs quarterly audits to ensure runbooks are accurate, dashboards exist, and alerts map to runbooks.

Appendix: Quick-check command snippets and helpful links
- kubectl, rollout and scaling commands (examples in runbook).
- Datadog/Grafana dashboards: <dashboard-links>.
- PagerDuty schedule: <pagerduty-link>.
- Incident templates: create a new Confluence page from this playbook and attach the incident timeline.
